label: task146-outbox-relay-marksent-cost
purpose: correct relay diagnostic timing (send/mark double-count on failure; split lockProcessing vs lockHold) and measure per-row markSent in-batch cost with a default-off bounded diagnostic; one bounded burst c100x2000 at default relay-interval-ms=5000 with diagnostics ON; NO markSent optimization applied

verdict.reason: TASK-146 only corrects the diagnostic timing and measures; no markSent optimization was implemented and no default value was changed. The single measured round used a DIFFERENT jar/diagnostic implementation than TASK-145, so its numbers are NOT an optimization before/after comparison.

nextSingleFactor.factor: per-row markSent internal cost composition (connection acquire / client JDBC execute / commit / server-side SQL / remaining client wait)
nextSingleFactor.measuredOuterBoundary: markSent is the largest locked segment: full-batch (rows=100) markMs P50 = 1053.5ms = 80.1% of lockProcessingMs P50 1314.5ms
nextSingleFactor.boundary: markMs is a mixed client wall clock (connection acquire + MyBatis/JDBC prepare-execute + network round trip + server-side UPDATE + commit/mapping). It must NOT be called pure server-side SQL, pure fsync, or pure pool wait.
nextSingleFactor.blocked: No safe, default-off, bounded instrumentation could be paired to the SAME markSent call without changing connection/transaction/exception semantics -> internal composition remains UNKNOWN; scope not expanded to force a conclusion.

singleRelayInstance.proof: diagnostic batch rows sum = success sum = 2010 = cohort; lockSkips = 0 throughout -> exactly one active relay instance delivered the whole cohort
